alerts.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued September 1 at 4:18PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
alerts.description:
HLSHGX

This product covers Southeast Texas

EDOUARD JUST INLAND ALONG THE NORTHWESTERN GULF COAST.

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Bolivar Peninsula,
Chambers, and Southern Liberty

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 60 miles northeast of Galveston TX
- 29.9N 94.0W
- Storm Intensity 50 mph
- Movement Northwest or 305 degrees at 7 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Edouard has moved inland along the Northwestern Gulf
Coast and is expected to continue to move further northwest across East
and Southeast Texas. The system's rainbands will continue to move
across Southeast Texas region through tonight and are expected to bring
periods of moderate to heavy rainfall with some showers and
thunderstorms potentially producing rainfall rates of 3-4 inches per
hour. Strong gusty winds can also be expected. This could lead to flash
flooding. Moreover, residual tropical moisture behind the system could
result in additional scattered moderate to heavy rainfall on Wednesday
as well.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Protect against life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
extensive impacts across portions of Southeast Texas. Potential
impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may
become dangerous rivers. Flood control systems and barriers may
become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Protect against dangerous rainfall flooding having possible limited
to significant impacts across portions of Southeast Texas.

* WIND:
Protect against hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
Chambers and Southern Liberty Counties. Potential impacts in this
area include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time across Southeast
Texas.

* TORNADOES:
Protect against a tornado event having possible limited impacts
across areas east of I-45. Potential impacts include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to complete all preparations to protect life and
property in accordance with your emergency plan. Ensure you are in a
safe location before the onset of strong winds or possible flooding.

Keep cell phones well charged. Cell phone chargers for automobiles
can be helpful, but be aware of your risk for deadly carbon monoxide
poisoning if your car is left idling in a garage or other poorly
ventilated area.

If you are a visitor, be sure to know the name of the city or town in
which you are staying and the name of the county or parish in which
it resides. Listen for these locations in local news updates. Pay
attention for instructions from local authorities.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather radio or local news outlets
for official storm information. Be ready to adapt to possible changes
to the forecast. Ensure you have multiple ways to receive weather
warnings.


* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Houston/Galveston TX around 10 PM CDT, or sooner if
conditions warrant.

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued September 1 at 3:54PM CDT until September 2 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
alerts.description:
Potential for Life Threatening Flash Flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Texas, including the following
areas, Bolivar Peninsula, Brazoria Islands, Brazos, Chambers,
Coastal Brazoria, Coastal Galveston, Coastal Harris, Fort Bend,
Galveston Island, Grimes, Houston, Inland Brazoria, Inland
Galveston, Inland Harris, Madison, Montgomery, Northern Liberty,
Polk, San Jacinto, Southern Liberty, Trinity, Walker and Waller.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- There is an increased danger to lives and property due to flash
flooding. Flash flooding is likely and considerable flash
flooding possible.

Periods of moderate to heavy rainfall associated with Tropical
Storm Edouard are expected to begin as early as this morning and
lasting into Wednesday evening. 3-6 inches with isolated amounts
up to 10-15 inches are expected with the highest totals occuring
along and east of I-45. Rainfall rates will exceed 3-4 inches per
hour at times in the heaviest downpours, which can lead to flash
flooding especially in urban and vulnerable areas.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

HLSHGX

This product covers Southeast Texas

AIR FORCE HURRICANE HUNTERS FIND EDOUARD IS STRENGTHENING AS IT
APPROACHES THE COAST NEAR THE TEXAS AND LOUISIANA BORDER.

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Bolivar Peninsula,
Chambers, and Southern Liberty

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 90 miles east of Galveston TX
- 29.4N 93.3W
- Storm Intensity 50 mph
- Movement Northwest or 305 degrees at 8 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Edouard is continuing to strengthen as it approaches
the Upper Texas Coast. The system's outer rainbands are moving further
inland into areas in and around Galveston Bay. These rainbands will
continue to push inland today and this evening. On the latest NHC
forecast track, the center of Edouard is forecast to move inland over
southeast Texas tonight. The primary concern for Southeast Texas
continues to be heavy rainfall. The heaviest showers and thunderstorms
could produce 3-4" per hour rainfall rates, which would result in flash
flooding. Residual tropical moisture could result in scattered heavy
showers and thunderstorms on Wednesday as well.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Protect against dangerous rainfall flooding having possible
significant impacts across Southeast Texas. Potential impacts
include:
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with swifter
currents and overspill their banks in a few places, especially
in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams, creeks, canals, and
ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken foundations.
Several places may experience expanded areas of rapid
inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Some streets and parking lots take on moving water as
storm drains and retention ponds overflow. Driving conditions
become hazardous. Some road and bridge closures.

Protect against locally hazardous rainfall flooding having possible
limited impacts across portions of Southeast Texas.

* WIND:
Protect against hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
Chambers and Southern Liberty Counties. Potential impacts in this
area include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Protect against locally hazardous surge having possible limited
impacts across Port Bolivar to High Island. Potential impacts in
this area include:
- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along
immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.
- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread
with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where
surge water covers the road.
- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly
in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.
- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,
and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* TORNADOES:
Protect against a tornado event having possible limited impacts
across areas east of I-45. Potential impacts include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to complete all preparations to protect life and
property in accordance with your emergency plan. Ensure you are in a
safe location before the onset of strong winds or possible flooding.

Keep cell phones well charged. Cell phone chargers for automobiles
can be helpful, but be aware of your risk for deadly carbon monoxide
poisoning if your car is left idling in a garage or other poorly
ventilated area.

If you are a visitor, be sure to know the name of the city or town in
which you are staying and the name of the county or parish in which
it resides. Listen for these locations in local news updates. Pay
attention for instructions from local authorities.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather radio or local news outlets
for official storm information. Be ready to adapt to possible changes
to the forecast. Ensure you have multiple ways to receive weather
warnings.


* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Houston/Galveston TX around 4 PM, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

alerts.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued September 1 at 4:17PM CDT until September 2 at 9:00AM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Strong rip currents are expected. Minor coastal
flooding and wave run-ups are possible north of Port Bolivar,
particularly during times of high tide.

* WHERE...Gulf-facing beaches,including Galveston Island and the
Bolivar Peninsula.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday morning.

isolated road closures possible, particularly for areas north
of Port Bolivar. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers
away from shore into deeper water.

alerts.headline: Tropical Storm Warning issued September 1 at 3:55PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
alerts.description:
* LOCATIONS AFFECTED
- Bolivar
- Crystal Beach
- High Island

* WIND
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Potential tropical storm force gusts.
- Peak Wind Forecast: 20-30 mph with gusts to 40 mph

- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST
UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Wind less than 39 mph
- The wind threat has remained nearly steady from the
previous assessment.
- PLAN: The sustained wind should remain less than tropical
storm force. Conditions may still be gusty.
- PREPARE: Listen for any instructions from local officials.
- ACT: Ensure emergency readiness should the forecast change.

- REALIZED IMPACTS: Being Assessed
- Little to no additional wind impacts expected. Community
officials are now assessing the extent of actual wind
impacts accordingly.

* STORM SURGE
- No storm surge inundation forecast

- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST
UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Little to no storm
surge flooding
- The storm surge threat has decreased from the previous
assessment.
- PLAN: The threat from storm surge is diminishing as flood
waters recede.
- PREPARE: Heed instructions from local officials when moving
about. Do not enter flooded areas.
- ACT: Exercise safety.

- REALIZED IMPACTS: Being Assessed
- Little to no additional surge impacts expected. Community
officials are now assessing the extent of actual surge
impacts accordingly.

* FLOODING RAIN
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Flood Watch is in effect
- Peak Rainfall Amounts: Additional around 1 inch

- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST
UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for
moderate flooding rain
- The flooding rain threat has remained nearly steady from
the previous assessment.
- PLAN: Emergency plans should include the potential for
moderate flooding from heavy rain. Evacuations and rescues
are possible.
- PREPARE: Consider protective actions if you are in an area
vulnerable to flooding.
- ACT: Heed any flood watches and warnings. Failure to take
action may result in serious injury or loss of life.

- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Significant
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations
and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with
swifter currents and overspill their banks in a few places,
especially in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams,
creeks, canals, and ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken
foundations. Several places may experience expanded areas
of rapid inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and
poor drainage areas. Some streets and parking lots take on
moving water as storm drains and retention ponds overflow.
Driving conditions become hazardous. Some road and bridge
closures.

* TORNADO
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST:
- Situation is unfavorable for tornadoes

- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST
UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Tornadoes not expected
- The tornado threat has remained nearly steady from the
previous assessment.
- PLAN: Tornadoes are not expected. Showers and thunderstorms
with gusty winds may still occur.
- PREPARE: Little to no preparations needed to protect
against tornadoes at this time. Keep informed of the latest
tornado situation.
- ACT: Listen for changes in the forecast.

- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Little to None
- Little to no potential impacts from tornadoes.

* FOR MORE INFORMATION:
- Hurricane Preparedness: Federal Emergency Management Agency
- http://ready.gov/hurricanes
- Local weather conditions and forecasts: NWS Houston/Galveston, TX
- http://www.weather.gov/hgx/

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

areas, Bolivar Peninsula, Brazoria Islands, Brazos, Chambers,

Galveston, Inland Harris, Madison, Montgomery, Northern Liberty,
Polk, San Jacinto, Southern Liberty, Trinity, Walker and Waller.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

- There is an increased danger to lives and property due to flash
flooding. Flash flooding is likely and considerable flash
flooding possible.

Storm Edouard are expected to begin as early as this morning and
lasting into Wednesday evening. 3-6 inches with isolated amounts
up to 10-15 inches are expected with the highest totals occuring
along and east of I-45. Rainfall rates will exceed 3-4 inches per
hour at times in the heaviest downpours, which can lead to flash
flooding especially in urban and vulnerable areas.

alerts.description:
Potential for Life Threatening Flash Flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Texas, including the following
areas, Bolivar Peninsula, Brazoria Islands, Brazos, Chambers,
Coastal Brazoria, Coastal Galveston, Coastal Harris, Fort Bend,
Galveston Island, Grimes, Houston, Inland Brazoria, Inland
Galveston, Inland Harris, Madison, Montgomery, Northern Liberty,
Polk, San Jacinto, Southern Liberty, Trinity, Walker and Waller.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- There is an increased danger to lives and property due to flash
flooding. Flash flooding is likely and considerable flash
flooding possible.

Periods of moderate to heavy rainfall associated with Tropical
Storm Edouard are expected to begin as early as this morning and
lasting into Wednesday evening. 3-6 inches with isolated amounts
up to 10-15 inches are expected with the highest totals occuring
along and east of I-45. Rainfall rates will exceed 3-4 inches per
hour at times in the heaviest downpours, which can lead to flash
flooding especially in urban and vulnerable areas.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

the Upper Texas Coast. The system's outer rainbands are moving further
inland into areas in and around Galveston Bay. These rainbands will
continue to push inland today and this evening. On the latest NHC
forecast track, the center of Edouard is forecast to move inland over
southeast Texas tonight. The primary concern for Southeast Texas
continues to be heavy rainfall. The heaviest showers and thunderstorms
could produce 3-4" per hour rainfall rates, which would result in flash
flooding. Residual tropical moisture could result in scattered heavy
showers and thunderstorms on Wednesday as well.

-----------------

Protect against dangerous rainfall flooding having possible
significant impacts across Southeast Texas. Potential impacts
include:
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with swifter
currents and overspill their banks in a few places, especially
in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams, creeks, canals, and
ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken foundations.

inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Some streets and parking lots take on moving water as
storm drains and retention ponds overflow. Driving conditions
become hazardous. Some road and bridge closures.

Protect against locally hazardous rainfall flooding having possible
limited impacts across portions of Southeast Texas.

Chambers and Southern Liberty Counties. Potential impacts in this
area include:

uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.

bridges and other elevated roadways.

alerts.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued September 1 at 4:49PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
alerts.description:
HLSLCH

This product covers Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas

**Tropical Storm Edouard Made Landfall Near Johnsons
Bayou **

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- The Tropical Storm Warning has been cancelled for Lower
Vermilion

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for East Cameron, Hardin,
Lower Jefferson, Northern Calcasieu, Northern Orange, Southern
Calcasieu, Southern Jasper, Southern Newton, Southern Orange,
Upper Jefferson, and West Cameron

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 20 miles north-northwest of Sabine Pass TX
- 29.9N 94.0W
- Storm Intensity 50 mph
- Movement Northwest or 305 degrees at 7 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Edouard officially made landfall near Johnsons
Bayou, LA, at 220 PM. The system will continue to weaken as it
moves inland. We received several reports of 50-60+ MPH wind gusts
across our coastal areas, with the highest being a gust to 71 MPH
at Texas Point shortly before landfall. The Hurricane Watch was
dropped earlier and replaced with a Tropical Storm Warning, while
the Storm Surge Warning was replaced with a Coastal Flood Warning
for lower Jefferson and western Cameron Parishes, along with a
Coastal Flood Advisory for southern Orange County, southern
Calcasieu, and eastern Cameron Parishes. Given that the coastal
threat has not entirely materialized and the system is now moving
inland, it is possible that the remaining coastal flood products
could be dropped over the next several hours.


POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

SETX/SWLA.

multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may

become stressed.

underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.

SETX/SWLA.

and communications disruptions.

toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and boats pulled
from moorings.

----------------------------------

Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Now is the time to stay inside and away from windows. Listen for
updates and be ready in case you lose electrical power. Keep a
battery-powered radio, charged cell phone and flashlight handy.


If you are prone to flooding or in an area under a storm surge watch
or warning, be prepared for the possibility of a quick and dramatic
rise in water levels.

If a tornado warning is issued for your area, quickly move to the
safest place within your shelter. Protect your head and body.

SETX.

immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Now is the time to stay inside and away from windows. Listen for
updates and be ready in case you lose electrical power. Keep a

If you are prone to flooding or in an area under a storm surge watch
or warning, be prepared for the possibility of a quick and dramatic
rise in water levels.

If a tornado warning is issued for your area, quickly move to the

alerts.description:
HLSLCH

This product covers Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas

**Tropical Storm Edouard Continues To Strengthen**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Storm Surge Warning, Tropical Storm Warning, and Hurricane
Watch are in effect for Lower Jefferson and West Cameron
- A Storm Surge Warning and Tropical Storm Warning are in effect
for East Cameron
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Hardin, Lower
Vermilion, Northern Calcasieu, Northern Orange, Southern
Calcasieu, Southern Jasper, Southern Newton, Southern Orange,
and Upper Jefferson

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 40 miles east-southeast of Sabine Pass TX
- 29.4N 93.3W
- Storm Intensity 50 mph
- Movement Northwest or 305 degrees at 8 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Edouard continues to track northwest offshore
of the southwest Louisiana Coast toward coastal southeast Texas or
extreme southwest Louisiana while becoming better organized. There
were no changes made to the watches and warnings that were already
in effect. Breezy conditions are ongoing, with some observations
along the coast gusting to 35 to 45 mph.

The forecast track remains largely unchanged with a landfall expected
near Sabine, TX. Flooding rainfall threat remains primarily along the
coastal parishes in southwest Louisiana and into Southeast Texas.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Potential impacts from the flooding rain are still unfolding across
SETX/SWLA.
If realized, these impacts include:
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with swifter
currents and overspill their banks in a few places, especially
in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams, creeks, canals, and
ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken foundations.
Several places may experience expanded areas of rapid
inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Some streets and parking lots take on moving water as
storm drains and retention ponds overflow. Driving conditions
become hazardous. Some road and bridge closures.


* SURGE:
Potential impacts from the main surge event are now unfolding across
SETX/SWLA.
If realized, these impacts include:
- Areas of inundation with storm surge flooding accentuated by
waves. Damage to several buildings, mainly near the coast.
- Sections of near-shore escape routes and secondary roads become
weakened or washed out, especially in usually vulnerable low
spots.
- Major beach erosion with heavy surf breaching dunes. Strong and
numerous rip currents.
- Moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks, and piers.
Several small craft broken away from moorings, especially in
unprotected anchorages.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
SETX/SWLA.
If realized, these impacts include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* TORNADOES:
Potential impacts from tornadoes are still unfolding across SETX/SWLA.
If realized, these impacts include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and boats pulled
from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Now is the time to stay inside and away from windows. Listen for
updates and be ready in case you lose electrical power. Keep a
battery-powered radio, charged cell phone and flashlight handy.


If you are prone to flooding or in an area under a storm surge watch
or warning, be prepared for the possibility of a quick and dramatic
rise in water levels.

If a tornado warning is issued for your area, quickly move to the
safest place within your shelter. Protect your head and body.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Lake Charles LA around 530 PM CDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

thunderstorms potentially producing rainfall rates of 3-4 inches per

alerts.description:
HLSLCH

This product covers Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas

**Tropical Storm Edouard Continues To Strengthen**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Storm Surge Warning, Tropical Storm Warning, and Hurricane
Watch are in effect for Lower Jefferson and West Cameron
- A Storm Surge Warning and Tropical Storm Warning are in effect
for East Cameron
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Hardin, Lower
Vermilion, Northern Calcasieu, Northern Orange, Southern
Calcasieu, Southern Jasper, Southern Newton, Southern Orange,
and Upper Jefferson

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 40 miles east-southeast of Sabine Pass TX
- 29.4N 93.3W
- Storm Intensity 50 mph
- Movement Northwest or 305 degrees at 8 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Edouard continues to track northwest offshore
of the southwest Louisiana Coast toward coastal southeast Texas or
extreme southwest Louisiana while becoming better organized. There
were no changes made to the watches and warnings that were already
in effect. Breezy conditions are ongoing, with some observations
along the coast gusting to 35 to 45 mph.

The forecast track remains largely unchanged with a landfall expected
near Sabine, TX. Flooding rainfall threat remains primarily along the
coastal parishes in southwest Louisiana and into Southeast Texas.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Potential impacts from the flooding rain are still unfolding across
SETX/SWLA.
If realized, these impacts include:
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with swifter
currents and overspill their banks in a few places, especially
in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams, creeks, canals, and
ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken foundations.
Several places may experience expanded areas of rapid
inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Some streets and parking lots take on moving water as
storm drains and retention ponds overflow. Driving conditions
become hazardous. Some road and bridge closures.


* SURGE:
Potential impacts from the main surge event are now unfolding across
SETX/SWLA.
If realized, these impacts include:
- Areas of inundation with storm surge flooding accentuated by
waves. Damage to several buildings, mainly near the coast.
- Sections of near-shore escape routes and secondary roads become
weakened or washed out, especially in usually vulnerable low
spots.
- Major beach erosion with heavy surf breaching dunes. Strong and
numerous rip currents.
- Moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks, and piers.
Several small craft broken away from moorings, especially in
unprotected anchorages.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
SETX/SWLA.
If realized, these impacts include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* TORNADOES:
Potential impacts from tornadoes are still unfolding across SETX/SWLA.
If realized, these impacts include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and boats pulled
from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Now is the time to stay inside and away from windows. Listen for
updates and be ready in case you lose electrical power. Keep a
battery-powered radio, charged cell phone and flashlight handy.


If you are prone to flooding or in an area under a storm surge watch
or warning, be prepared for the possibility of a quick and dramatic
rise in water levels.

If a tornado warning is issued for your area, quickly move to the
safest place within your shelter. Protect your head and body.

- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

-----------

Service in Lake Charles LA around 530 PM CDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

extensive impacts across portions of Southeast Texas. Potential

multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may
become dangerous rivers. Flood control systems and barriers may
become stressed.

communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.

to significant impacts across portions of Southeast Texas.

area include:

uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.

or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Texas.

of emergency plans during tropical events.

and communications disruptions.

toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

safe location before the onset of strong winds or possible flooding.

can be helpful, but be aware of your risk for deadly carbon monoxide
poisoning if your car is left idling in a garage or other poorly
ventilated area.

it resides. Listen for these locations in local news updates. Pay
attention for instructions from local authorities.

for official storm information. Be ready to adapt to possible changes
to the forecast. Ensure you have multiple ways to receive weather
warnings.

- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

waves. Damage to several buildings, mainly near the coast.

weakened or washed out, especially in usually vulnerable low
spots.

numerous rip currents.

uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.

large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and boats pulled

rise in water levels.

alerts.description:
AQAFWD

The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has issued
an Ozone Action Day for the Dallas-Fort Worth area for Tuesday,
September 1, 2026.

Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing
high levels of ozone air pollution in the Dallas-Fort Worth area
on Tuesday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by sharing a
ride, walking, riding a bicycle, taking your lunch to work,
avoiding drive-through lanes, conserving energy, and keeping your
vehicle properly tuned.

alerts.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued September 1 at 4:18PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
alerts.description:
HLSHGX

This product covers Southeast Texas

EDOUARD JUST INLAND ALONG THE NORTHWESTERN GULF COAST.

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Bolivar Peninsula,
Chambers, and Southern Liberty

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 60 miles northeast of Galveston TX
- 29.9N 94.0W
- Storm Intensity 50 mph
- Movement Northwest or 305 degrees at 7 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Edouard has moved inland along the Northwestern Gulf
Coast and is expected to continue to move further northwest across East
and Southeast Texas. The system's rainbands will continue to move
across Southeast Texas region through tonight and are expected to bring
periods of moderate to heavy rainfall with some showers and
thunderstorms potentially producing rainfall rates of 3-4 inches per
hour. Strong gusty winds can also be expected. This could lead to flash
flooding. Moreover, residual tropical moisture behind the system could
result in additional scattered moderate to heavy rainfall on Wednesday
as well.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Protect against life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
extensive impacts across portions of Southeast Texas. Potential
impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may
become dangerous rivers. Flood control systems and barriers may
become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Protect against dangerous rainfall flooding having possible limited
to significant impacts across portions of Southeast Texas.

* WIND:
Protect against hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
Chambers and Southern Liberty Counties. Potential impacts in this
area include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time across Southeast
Texas.

* TORNADOES:
Protect against a tornado event having possible limited impacts
across areas east of I-45. Potential impacts include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to complete all preparations to protect life and
property in accordance with your emergency plan. Ensure you are in a
safe location before the onset of strong winds or possible flooding.

Keep cell phones well charged. Cell phone chargers for automobiles
can be helpful, but be aware of your risk for deadly carbon monoxide
poisoning if your car is left idling in a garage or other poorly
ventilated area.

If you are a visitor, be sure to know the name of the city or town in
which you are staying and the name of the county or parish in which
it resides. Listen for these locations in local news updates. Pay
attention for instructions from local authorities.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather radio or local news outlets
for official storm information. Be ready to adapt to possible changes
to the forecast. Ensure you have multiple ways to receive weather
warnings.


* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Houston/Galveston TX around 10 PM CDT, or sooner if
conditions warrant.

alerts.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued September 1 at 10:34AM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
alerts.description:
HLSHGX

This product covers Southeast Texas

AIR FORCE HURRICANE HUNTERS FIND EDOUARD IS STRENGTHENING AS IT
APPROACHES THE COAST NEAR THE TEXAS AND LOUISIANA BORDER.

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Bolivar Peninsula,
Chambers, and Southern Liberty

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 90 miles east of Galveston TX
- 29.4N 93.3W
- Storm Intensity 50 mph
- Movement Northwest or 305 degrees at 8 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Edouard is continuing to strengthen as it approaches
the Upper Texas Coast. The system's outer rainbands are moving further
inland into areas in and around Galveston Bay. These rainbands will
continue to push inland today and this evening. On the latest NHC
forecast track, the center of Edouard is forecast to move inland over
southeast Texas tonight. The primary concern for Southeast Texas
continues to be heavy rainfall. The heaviest showers and thunderstorms
could produce 3-4" per hour rainfall rates, which would result in flash
flooding. Residual tropical moisture could result in scattered heavy
showers and thunderstorms on Wednesday as well.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Protect against dangerous rainfall flooding having possible
significant impacts across Southeast Texas. Potential impacts
include:
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with swifter
currents and overspill their banks in a few places, especially
in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams, creeks, canals, and
ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken foundations.
Several places may experience expanded areas of rapid
inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Some streets and parking lots take on moving water as
storm drains and retention ponds overflow. Driving conditions
become hazardous. Some road and bridge closures.

Protect against locally hazardous rainfall flooding having possible
limited impacts across portions of Southeast Texas.

* WIND:
Protect against hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
Chambers and Southern Liberty Counties. Potential impacts in this
area include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Protect against locally hazardous surge having possible limited
impacts across Port Bolivar to High Island. Potential impacts in
this area include:
- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along
immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.
- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread
with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where
surge water covers the road.
- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly
in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.
- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,
and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* TORNADOES:
Protect against a tornado event having possible limited impacts
across areas east of I-45. Potential impacts include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to complete all preparations to protect life and
property in accordance with your emergency plan. Ensure you are in a
safe location before the onset of strong winds or possible flooding.

Keep cell phones well charged. Cell phone chargers for automobiles
can be helpful, but be aware of your risk for deadly carbon monoxide
poisoning if your car is left idling in a garage or other poorly
ventilated area.

If you are a visitor, be sure to know the name of the city or town in
which you are staying and the name of the county or parish in which
it resides. Listen for these locations in local news updates. Pay
attention for instructions from local authorities.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather radio or local news outlets
for official storm information. Be ready to adapt to possible changes
to the forecast. Ensure you have multiple ways to receive weather
warnings.


* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Houston/Galveston TX around 4 PM, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

alerts.description:

This product covers Southeast Texas

AIR FORCE HURRICANE HUNTERS FIND EDOUARD IS STRENGTHENING AS IT
APPROACHES THE COAST NEAR THE TEXAS AND LOUISIANA BORDER.

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Bolivar Peninsula,
Chambers, and Southern Liberty

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 90 miles east of Galveston TX
- 29.4N 93.3W
- Storm Intensity 50 mph
- Movement Northwest or 305 degrees at 8 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Edouard is continuing to strengthen as it approaches
the Upper Texas Coast. The system's outer rainbands are moving further
inland into areas in and around Galveston Bay. These rainbands will
continue to push inland today and this evening. On the latest NHC
forecast track, the center of Edouard is forecast to move inland over
southeast Texas tonight. The primary concern for Southeast Texas
continues to be heavy rainfall. The heaviest showers and thunderstorms
could produce 3-4" per hour rainfall rates, which would result in flash
flooding. Residual tropical moisture could result in scattered heavy
showers and thunderstorms on Wednesday as well.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Protect against dangerous rainfall flooding having possible
significant impacts across Southeast Texas. Potential impacts
include:
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with swifter
currents and overspill their banks in a few places, especially
in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams, creeks, canals, and
ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken foundations.
Several places may experience expanded areas of rapid
inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Some streets and parking lots take on moving water as
storm drains and retention ponds overflow. Driving conditions
become hazardous. Some road and bridge closures.

Protect against locally hazardous rainfall flooding having possible
limited impacts across portions of Southeast Texas.

* WIND:
Protect against hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
Chambers and Southern Liberty Counties. Potential impacts in this
area include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Protect against locally hazardous surge having possible limited
impacts across Port Bolivar to High Island. Potential impacts in
this area include:
- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along
immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.
- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread
with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where
surge water covers the road.
- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly
in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.
- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,
and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* TORNADOES:
Protect against a tornado event having possible limited impacts
across areas east of I-45. Potential impacts include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to complete all preparations to protect life and
property in accordance with your emergency plan. Ensure you are in a
safe location before the onset of strong winds or possible flooding.

Keep cell phones well charged. Cell phone chargers for automobiles
can be helpful, but be aware of your risk for deadly carbon monoxide
poisoning if your car is left idling in a garage or other poorly
ventilated area.

If you are a visitor, be sure to know the name of the city or town in
which you are staying and the name of the county or parish in which
it resides. Listen for these locations in local news updates. Pay
attention for instructions from local authorities.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather radio or local news outlets
for official storm information. Be ready to adapt to possible changes
to the forecast. Ensure you have multiple ways to receive weather
warnings.


* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Houston/Galveston TX around 4 PM, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued September 1 at 3:54PM CDT until September 2 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
alerts.description:
Potential for Life Threatening Flash Flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Texas, including the following
areas, Bolivar Peninsula, Brazoria Islands, Brazos, Chambers,
Coastal Brazoria, Coastal Galveston, Coastal Harris, Fort Bend,
Galveston Island, Grimes, Houston, Inland Brazoria, Inland
Galveston, Inland Harris, Madison, Montgomery, Northern Liberty,
Polk, San Jacinto, Southern Liberty, Trinity, Walker and Waller.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- There is an increased danger to lives and property due to flash
flooding. Flash flooding is likely and considerable flash
flooding possible.

Periods of moderate to heavy rainfall associated with Tropical
Storm Edouard are expected to begin as early as this morning and
lasting into Wednesday evening. 3-6 inches with isolated amounts
up to 10-15 inches are expected with the highest totals occuring
along and east of I-45. Rainfall rates will exceed 3-4 inches per
hour at times in the heaviest downpours, which can lead to flash
flooding especially in urban and vulnerable areas.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
